name: Everglades Ops

question: Where are Burmese pythons active and where should removal crews go next?

score.label: Hotspot score (density x activity x access, labelled heuristic)

components.label: Recent sightings
components.description: Kernel density of recent python sightings (21-day half-life); NAS and GBIF history as a static prior.

components.label: Activity rules

legend.sightings: One dot per report; duplicates and ID conflicts are flagged, never hidden.
legend.hotspots: Score per 0.02 degree cell; brighter is higher. A heuristic, not a probability.
legend.lst: GOES-19 land surface temperature, hatched where cloud or bad quality.
legend.sst: GOES-19 sea surface temperature; buoys may disagree.
legend.stations: USGS gauges, NDBC buoys and CO-OPS tide stations with their latest reading.
legend.alerts: NWS products in effect at the cursor time.
legend.missions: Areas the team has claimed or finished.
legend.peers: Teammates on the board right now.
legend.notes: Field notes pinned to the map.

copy.about: A live map of Burmese python reports in South Florida, from sightings people report to iNaturalist and wildlife agencies, with an agent you can ask about them.
copy.legendTitle: Burmese pythons reported in South Florida
copy.title: Everglades Ops
copy.sightingsNote: Sightings are reports, not abundance: more observers mean more reports.
copy.scopeNote: South Florida and the Keys only.

agent.persona: You are the operations analyst for Everglades python removal crews. You answer from the stored sightings, readings, alerts, forecasts and hotspot scores of South Florida, cite every number, and state feed freshness.
agent.scope: Burmese python in South Florida and the Keys (west -83.2, south 24.3, east -79.8, north 27.5). No other species is tracked here.
agent.refusal: Everglades Ops answers for Burmese pythons only, in South Florida and the Keys; it tracks no other species. Switch to Lionfish Watch for lionfish or to the Carp app for Louisiana rivers.
